柬埔寨木琴音色明亮清脆，具有溫潤的木質感。其音域為中音域，音高清晰而富有穿透力。: The Cambodian xylophone has a bright, clear timbre with a warm, woody quality. Its range is the middle register, and its pitch is clear and penetrating. The instrument is made of wooden bars with resonating tubes beneath, which produce a warm, full resonance and give the sound depth. Beside the deep, heavy tone of the marimba, the Cambodian xylophone is lighter and more agile; beside the dry quality of the African xylophone, it sounds gentler and rounder. Struck quickly, the notes come out distinct and clear, with good phrasing; played slowly, it has a calm, elegant air. The instrument's sound is transparent overall, and it particularly suits the complex rhythmic textures of traditional Khmer music.

柬埔寨鐵琴為體鳴金屬琴，起源可能早於安哥拉時期，或與早期安哥拉時期相關。另有柬埔: The roneat dek is an idiophone of struck metal bars; its origin may predate the Angkor period or be connected with the early Angkor period. Ouknha Moha Thipadei Meas Ni, head of the Cambodian royal ensemble, also states that this kind of roneat evolved from the Javanese gamelan instrument gendér, and that this is connected with Jayavarman II's exile in Java at the end of the ninth century and his return to found the Khmer Empire; the form has since departed markedly from the original gendér. An important change is that roneat thong and roneat dek may be the same instrument: the former, with gold-bronze bars, was used in the palace, the latter, with iron bars, in ensembles outside the palace, at picnics or in temples.
柬埔寨鐵琴的發聲體為二十一條黑色鐵條；變體 Roneat Thong 則使用紅褐: The sounding body of the roneat dek is twenty-one black iron bars; the variant Roneat Thong uses red-brown brass or bronze bars, close to gold in colour. Because of their weight the bars cannot be suspended; instead they are laid out by scale on pads on a rectangular resonating trough. The beaters are made of a hard material; the source mentions buffalo hide or elephant hide. The materials of the resonating trough, the pads and the other parts are not stated.
柬埔寨鐵琴（Roneat dek）為東南亞柬埔寨的金屬體鳴樂器，與柬埔寨木琴 R: The roneat dek is a metal idiophone from Cambodia in Southeast Asia, close to the Cambodian xylophone roneat ek. It is built of 21 black iron or bronze bars; because of their weight they cannot be suspended, so they are laid out by scale on pads on a rectangular resonating trough and tuned by scraping or burning away some of the metal. The player strikes them with a pair of hard beaters. The instrument is used in the pinpeat ensemble and the mohori orchestra, and is also found outside the palace or on temple occasions.
站於琴前，雙手持棒敲擊琴鍵中央。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使: Stand in front of the instrument and strike the middle of the keys with a stick in each hand. You hold the instrument itself and make it vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking. Different parts and different amounts of force give different timbres. In practice, first confirm the correct way of holding the instrument, and once the basic way of sounding it is in hand, go on to rhythms and melodies. Fingers or drumsticks strike the surface and the bounce brings them back naturally, with the wrist relaxed.
